compiler: emcc (Emscripten gcc/clang-like replacement + linker emulating GNU ld) 3.1.74 (1092ec30a3fb1d46b1782ff1b4db5094d3d06ae5)
scope: Lab-built wasm32 modules of Android's public-key / TLS native layer, from the official AOSP sources at android-13.0.0_r1. Never derived from an APK or from a device binary.

boringssl.built: sources.bp libcrypto_sources + libcrypto_bcm_sources (libcrypto.so), libssl_sources (libssl.so); portable C, OPENSSL_NO_ASM

linkFlags: -O2 -sSIDE_MODULE=1 -sWASM_BIGINT=1 -fwasm-exceptions -Wl,--gc-sections; DT_NEEDED rewritten to the Android order
labGlue: scripts/wasm/javacrypto/apkweb-sysrand.c (the operating-system entropy layer of crypto/fipsmodule/rand, replacing urandom.c: crypto.getRandomValues through apkweb_javacrypto.random_fill)
scripts/wasm/javacrypto/patch-native-crypto.py (NativeCrypto_HMAC_Init_ex takes the long EVP_MD pointer as jlong, not jobject: a 32-bit-ABI signature fix, behaviour unchanged)
entropy: Every random byte BoringSSL draws (RAND_bytes, key generation, blinding, nonces) comes from CRYPTO_sysrand -> apkweb_javacrypto.random_fill -> crypto.getRandomValues. The import throws when WebCrypto is unavailable; there is no clock- or counter-derived fallback.
deviations: the FIPS-validated libcrypto of the device (BORINGSSL_FIPS, bcm module integrity check) is not built: wasm has no module-in-place integrity check; the algorithms are the same BoringSSL sources
portable C implementations (OPENSSL_NO_ASM) instead of the arm64/x86_64 assembly
crypto/fipsmodule/rand/urandom.c is replaced by apkweb-sysrand.c in a build-local copy of bcm.c (entropy source only)
single-threaded wasm: BoringSSL locks are the libc stubs of the shared base module
